I farm 24 mu, but my main system is still wheat-maize, so I will keep most of the land in that familiar rotation and leave a smaller part for cotton. My household has only 2 people and some labor goes off-farm, so I will not spread myself too thin with too much cotton because cotton takes more hand management over a long season. I have 30 years of farming experience and well irrigation, so I will rely on improved or hybrid seed and steady but not excessive fertilizer, with enough water at the key stages. I will put 18 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 18 mu, and 6 mu into cotton in spring. For wheat, I will aim for stable tillering and grain filling with moderate nitrogen and two irrigations. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer stronger than wheat, and irrigate when summer rain is not enough. For cotton, I will keep the area smaller, use improved seed, control fertilizer so the crop does not grow too rank, irrigate a few times from the well, and spray as needed because insects are usually a bigger concern there. I am choosing this plan because it fits my labor, matches my land and irrigation conditions, and gives me a balance between grain security and cash income.
